newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up on hopes of further gains.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up on hopes of further gains.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Friday on speculative buying by local operators hoping for a price rise and higher volumes next week, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 21 shares rose 0.93 to 182.64 on volume of $10.71 million.

"Why should we not speculate on a rise, if all the preconditions are there for that?" said Ilya Galtsov, a trader from Trinfiko brokerage. "All cheap shares have already been purchased and there may be a rise in prices and volumes on Tuesday." Monday is often quiet.
Lenenergo was the gainer of the day with shares rising to $0.40/$0.47 from $0.36/$0.37 at Thursday's close.
Galtsov said the shares rose on the news that Lenenergo plans talks in early September with Veba AG's Preussenelektra utility on cooperation and joint projects.
He said there was much interest in regional telecoms and electricity companies' shares, as these firms show good financial results.
Traders said that they expected prices to rise next week after most Western investors come back from the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
"The trend is in the upside and will stay like this in the course of September," said Nikolay Mokhoff, sales director from Alliance-Menatep.
Mosenerg closed at $0.975/$0.980 after $0.963/$0.969 at Thursday's close, LUKoil rose to $9.90/$9.97 from $9.77/$9.87 and Surgutneftegaz edged up to $0.425/$0.428 from $0.412/$0.419.
